shared_elements: upright stone slab/monolith with rounded or damaged top
low-relief carving on a single flat face
circle or disc motif set centrally
horizontal incised bands dividing the surface into zones
paired, roughly symmetrical curving forms flanking a centre
justification: Both are upright, roughly rounded-topped stone monuments carved in low relief on one face, each with a prominent disc and horizontal incised divisions separating an upper figural zone from a lower one, which gives a broadly comparable silhouette and top-to-bottom zoning. The rendering, however, is quite different: B is a crisp, ruled, register-based composition with dense rows of small script signs and finely modelled standing figures, whereas A is coarse, eroded, script-free and built from large curvilinear bosses and swelling volumes wrapped over a thick block.
